comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DEEP-DIVE (2026-08-18): impact of replacing the write path with single-source-of-truth + generation (Pattern A). Grounded in _lib_writes.py, _mcp_writes.py, _commands/claim.py, close_disposition.py, schemas/gen_types.py, schemas/check_mcp_models.py.

BASELINE — what is already single-sourced vs not:
- BEHAVIOR is already SSOT. All surfaces (lib rebar.*, CLI, MCP tools) funnel into ONE core: composer.create_core / transition.transition_compute / claim_compute. Validation, gating, concurrency, event emission, close-disposition all live once. The lib functions and MCP tools are thin adapters.
- Only the PARAM DECLARATION + surface adaptation is hand-mirrored across surfaces.
- Existing generation discipline covers OUTPUT/return shapes ONLY (gen_types = schemas -> TypedDicts codegen, drift-gated; check_mcp_models = one-way missing-property check on 10 output models). There are NO input schemas for write ops.
- CORRECTION to earlier note: there is NO NDJSON ticket-write surface. "Import" is the source= provenance kwarg on create_ticket, not a separate validated surface. The real surfaces are lib / CLI / MCP.

GOTCHAS — where naive "generate the surfaces" would REGRESS:
G1 Deliberate policy divergence (no-force over MCP). transition_ticket/claim_ticket INTENTIONALLY omit force/force_close/reason/caused_by/ref (documented: "intentionally NO force bypass over MCP"). Generating from one param model would either expose force over MCP (real policy/security regression: unaudited gate bypass by agents) or require per-field surface-visibility annotations. Intended divergence is first-class, not drift.
G2 Adapter-bound params that must never be caller-visible: _creation_channel (hardcoded python/cli/mcp), return_alias (hardcoded True in MCP; a Python ergonomic), source (import-only), repo_root (lib-only; CLI derives from cwd, MCP from server ctx). Naive generation leaks these onto surfaces.
G3 Per-surface type/ergonomics carry BEHAVIOR. The CLI is a HAND-ROLLED arg loop (not argparse) with semantics like: bare --force -> default reason "(no reason given)"; --assignee ABSENT = None sentinel (-> default_assignee fallback) vs explicit --assignee "" = clear. MCP uses pydantic + LLM-facing docstrings (the description IS the contract the model reads). A uniform generated parser loses these bespoke rules (regression) or needs per-field custom hooks (defeats generation).
G4 THE REAL PARITY RISK IS BEHAVIORAL, and generation cannot express it. close_class defaults to '' on EVERY surface, but "required" is a RUNTIME rule: required iff ticket_type==bug AND target==closed; and reason is conditionally required/persisted (admits_close_reason: only a non-force close whose class is in REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES {obsolete,wontfix,not_a_bug,escalated}). Cross-field, data-dependent semantics can't live in a param schema. A generated surface would look identical yet still diverge on exactly what this ticket cares about -> false confidence.
G5 Return contract is bivalent by param (create_ticket @overload return_alias False->str / True->CreateResult; MCP hardcodes True). A generator must not reproduce overloads on CLI/MCP.
G6 Migration blast radius. Regenerating the CLI risks changing flag spellings/help/the exit-code contract (10=concurrency); regenerating MCP changes the LLM-facing tool schema (breaks agent prompts / cached tool defs). These are user/agent-visible contracts — high blast radius for a change whose behavioral core is ALREADY unified.
G7 Open-vs-closed mismatch reappears. gen_types already had to emit CLOSED TypedDicts from OPEN (additionalProperties:true) schemas. Input side is the same: the core takes evolving kwargs while CLI/MCP inputs are closed. Authoring input schemas re-introduces that tension + a new drift gate + schema-authoring burden.
G8 check_mcp_models is one-directional (missing-property only), output-only. Reused for inputs it inherits blind spots (no type/required/extra checks); making it bidirectional would immediately flag the G1 deliberate omissions as drift, forcing an intended-divergence declaration anyway.

CONCLUSION: the write path is NOT a fit for full "generate the surfaces" Pattern A. Unlike FastAPI/protobuf (surfaces are pure projections), rebar's surfaces carry irreducible INTENDED per-surface behavior (G1-G3) and the true risk is RUNTIME/behavioral (G4) which generation cannot capture. Behavior is already SSOT, so generating param declarations buys little safety at large blast radius (G6).

RECOMMENDED (fitted, low-risk) — two complementary, scoped pieces, NOT full codegen:
(1) One declared param model per write op as SSOT, each field annotated with its surfaces (e.g. force: {cli, lib}; _creation_channel: adapter-bound), enforced by a --check DRIFT GATE in the check_mcp_models style but bidirectional + input-side. It CHECKS, does not generate — hand-written adapters stay (preserving G3 ergonomics + G6 contracts). Catches accidental drift (a new core param nobody surfaced) and refuses accidental exposure of an adapter-bound/omitted field. Intended divergence is declared IN the model, not an external allow-list.
(2) A SCOPED behavioral conformance test for the runtime conditional-required rules (G4) ONLY: a small accept/reject matrix (e.g. bug-close missing close_class -> rejected on both CLI and MCP; reason-required class missing --reason -> rejected) run through each adapter. This is the one place a behavioral test (not a shape gate) is the right tool, scoped to the conditional rules, not a general parity matrix.

This supersedes the earlier "generation + conformance + allow-list" blend: for rebar's write path it is CHECK-not-generate (the SSOT drift gate) + a narrowly-scoped behavioral test for the rules a schema cannot hold.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
DECISION REVISITED + FINALIZED (2026-08-18, supersedes the deep-dive's "check-not-generate + scoped test" recommendation). Two operator rulings collapsed the remaining ambiguity:

RULING 1 — force through ANY surface, audited by the ABSENCE of a signed attestation. A force op produces no signed attestation (gate bypassed / closed-without-signature); that missing signature IS the durable audit signal, and projects that want to prevent force from circumventing protections check for certification in their CI pipeline. Consequence: MCP must GAIN force parity; the prior "force is CLI-only" governance is RESCINDED. This removes the last "intended divergence".
RULING 2 — to keep parity exception-free, REMOVE deprecated flags/verbs that would fail the oracle rather than exempt them. So force_close (deprecated) is NOT mirrored to MCP and NOT given an oracle exception — it is removed from the input surface. Same principle for any other deprecated write verb/flag.

NET: the write-op param surface has ZERO intended divergences. The oracle asserts TOTAL parity across lib / CLI / MCP with NO capability flags and NO allow-list. This is the cleanest form of the OSS conformance-oracle pattern and fully retires the earlier Frankenstein risk (no generation+conformance+allow-list blend).

MECHANISM (Pattern B — behavioral conformance oracle, a single proven OSS pattern):
- ONE transport-agnostic behavioral contract = a table of (op, inputs, expected accept/reject + expected effect). Run it through each adapter (lib, CLI, MCP) against a temp store. Precedent: DB-API / SQLAlchemy dialect compliance, CommonMark spec suite, WSGI/ASGI validators, S3-compat & k8s CRI/CSI conformance suites.
- It tests BEHAVIOR/CONTRACT (accept/reject/effect), so it catches the real risk (G4 runtime conditional-required rules: close_class required iff bug-close; reason conditionally required per REASON_REQUIRED_CLASSES) that shape-generation provably cannot. It is NOT a change-detector and NOT an NxM matrix: one authored contract, N adapters; new adapter reruns the same suite; new op adds one spec row; drift in ANY adapter fails automatically.
- Divergence == a FAILING conformance case (a bug to converge), not an allow-listed exception.

WHY NOT Pattern A (generate the surfaces): behavior is ALREADY single-sourced (all surfaces funnel into composer.create_core / transition_compute / claim_compute), so codegen buys little; the surfaces carry irreducible hand-written value (LLM-facing MCP docstrings; CLI ergonomics); generation CANNOT express the runtime conditional-required rules (G4); and regenerating CLI/MCP would risk user/agent-visible contract breaks (flag spellings, exit code 10, LLM tool schema). Pattern A is retired for the write path.

REMEDIATION (proposed split-out tickets, discovered_from cranial-goodly-seahog):
1. MCP write-param parity BUG — transition_ticket/claim_ticket gain force + reason + caused_by + ref (NOT force_close). Update the MCP docstrings that assert "intentionally NO force bypass".
2. Behavioral conformance ORACLE — the accept/reject+effect suite over lib/CLI/MCP adapters, temp-store driven, zero exceptions. This is the durable parity gate.
3. Remove deprecated write-path surface — force_close (and any deprecated verb/flag) via the supported rebar._deprecations tombstone/warn path. CAVEAT (event-sourcing): force_close lives in the EVENT SCHEMA + reducer (ticket_state.schema.json, _processors_status.py, txn.py) — remove the INPUT surface (lib param, CLI close --force) but the reducer must keep tolerating historical force_close events (tombstone, NOT hard delete).
4. CLI standardization (SEPARATE, orthogonal) — the CLI is a hand-rolled arg loop (bespoke --force default-reason, --assignee None-sentinel-vs-clear). Move toward a standard framework (argparse/Click/Typer) for consistency + accurate --help, as maintained OSS CLIs do. This is an ADAPTER refactor; the oracle then simply validates the new CLI too. It does NOT blend with the oracle (avoids Frankenstein).
5. Docs — rewrite AGENTS.md's "--force is CLI-only / not exposed over MCP" governance to the new model (force everywhere; audit = absent attestation; projects gate on certification in CI).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
EXPERIMENT — behavioral conformance-oracle PROTOTYPE run (2026-08-18). Validated Pattern B empirically against a temp store; artifact: docs/experiments/write_parity_oracle_prototype.py. Reused the tests' _FakeMCP/_FakeCtx capture + the interfaces sandbox-repo bootstrap; ran identical behavioral cases through the lib adapter (rebar.transition) and the MCP adapter (captured transition_ticket callable), classifying each as ACCEPTED / REJECTED(runtime rule) / PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED(surface can't express the input).

RESULTS (case -> lib | mcp):
A bug-close MISSING close_class        -> REJECTED | REJECTED   [PARITY — runtime "required iff bug-close" rule enforced on both]
B reason-required class, no reason     -> REJECTED | REJECTED   [PARITY]
C COMPLIANT not_a_bug close (w/ reason)-> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]
D caused_by culprit attribution        -> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]
E force start-work bypass (open->in_progress) -> ACCEPTED | PARAM_NOT_EXPOSED   [GAP]

KEY FINDINGS:
1. The oracle flagged EXACTLY the three real gaps (MCP transition_ticket lacks reason, caused_by, force) and NOTHING spurious. Contrast the earlier naive signature-parity experiment, which fired on 4/5 ops with FALSE-POSITIVES (force_close/source/return_alias/_creation_channel) and was BLIND to the runtime close_class rule. The behavioral oracle inverts both failure modes: no false-positives, and it directly exercises the runtime rule.
2. The A->C trap is the concrete bug: MCP REJECTS a bug-close demanding --reason (B) yet cannot SUPPLY it (C). An agent on MCP is told to provide something the surface can't express -> a compliant reason-required bug close is UNREACHABLE over MCP today. Same shape for caused_by (D) and force (E).
3. Cases A/B prove the oracle verifies BEHAVIOR a shape/signature gate cannot: close_class is default '' on BOTH surfaces, yet the required-iff-bug-close rule is checked at runtime and both surfaces are confirmed to honor it.
4. force_close was deliberately NOT tested (deprecated, being removed per Ruling 2) — so the oracle carries zero exceptions and still catches everything real.

CONCLUSION: Pattern B (behavioral conformance oracle) is validated. It is the correct single mechanism: exception-free, false-positive-free, and it catches the runtime conditional-required rules generation cannot. The prototype IS the seed of the durable oracle (remediation ticket 2). The three gaps it cataloged ARE the MCP-parity bug (remediation ticket 1): add reason + caused_by + force to transition_ticket (claim_ticket gets force too).

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
## Force/reason surface audit + ruling (A) — normalization design (2026-08-18)

Operator rulings this session, in order, converged on:
- `--force[=<reason>]` is THE universal approved write pattern. The audit reason is tightly coupled to the force operation (it belongs on the audit record), so it rides INLINE on `--force`, NOT on a separate `--reason`. This REVERSED an interim decoupling proposal.
- `force_close` is to be REMOVED (its force-close audit reason is carried by `--force=<reason>` on a close).
- `force` is allowed through any command surface; auditability comes from the fact that a force op yields NO signed attestation (projects can gate on certification in CI).
- Blast radius for this normalization is limited to **transition + claim** (both externally-exposed surfaces — lib/CLI/MCP — AND internal module/method naming, AND transition/claim guidance text). tracker-maintenance / init / gates break-glass `--force` for OTHER commands are OUT of scope.

### Canonical model: `claim` already has the target shape
lib `claim(force: str | None = None)` — the value IS the audit reason; bare CLI `--force` -> "(no reason given)", `--force=<reason>` -> that reason. Everything else normalizes to this.

### Audit findings (the divergences to fix)
1. **transition lib** splits one concept across `force: bool` + separate `reason: str` + redundant `force_close: str|None` (_lib_writes.py ~228-240). Target: `force: str | None` like claim; drop bool + force_close.
2. **transition CLI** lets `--reason` stand in as the force-bypass note (transition.py help ~42-46, 59-63) — a coupling claim lacks. Target: force note from `--force=<reason>` only; `--reason` = close_reason only.
3. **Internal naming drift** — the single "force-bypass reason" concept is spelled 4 ways: `force_reason` (CLI _parse_flags), `force_close` (lib param), `force_close_reason` (txn.py plumbing + a PERSISTED status_data key, txn.py ~197/250/318/371-372), `force_plan_review` (claim_compute). Target: unify IN-MEMORY names to `force_reason`; RETAIN the persisted `force_close_reason` status key (durable reduced state; renaming = event-schema migration, out of scope).
4. **Guidance text** — gates.py (~302-303) prints two spellings in one override hint: `claim --force="<reason>"` AND the decoupled `transition --force --reason="<reason>"`. Target: unify both to `--force[=<reason>]`. (txn.py override hints ~554/602/618 already show `--force="<reason>"`.)
5. **Close-gate keying** — the completion-verify close gate keys on `force_close` specifically (close_precheck.py ~566, transition_close.py ~440), NOT on `force`. Consolidating requires rewiring these to `force is not None`.
6. **MCP** transition_ticket/claim_ticket lack force/reason/caused_by/ref (docstrings assert a now-void no-force policy). Handled by sibling scratchy-leprous-galago (already certified); MCP `force` follows the same reason-carrying str.

### Migration / back-compat
- lib `force_close="<r>"` -> WARN via the sanctioned lib-kind deprecation alias (_deprecations `_KINDS` includes `lib`) and map to `force="<r>"`; `force=True` -> `force="(no reason given)"`. There is no lib/cli hard-tombstone (only env/cfg/file tombstone), so a warn+map alias is the correct retirement path for the kwarg.
- Reducer/schema UNCHANGED: historical events (incl. `force_close_reason` status field) reduce to identical state.

### Ticket mapping (all discovered_from cranial-goodly-seahog)
- blusterous-earthly-kitten (task) — the normalization above (lib + CLI + guidance + internal naming; remove force_close). Foundational.
- churlish-fruited-dassie (story, depends_on blusterous) — mechanical argparse refactor preserving the POST-blusterous `--force[=<reason>]` surface.
- topaz-blubbery-mice (story) — Pattern-B conformance oracle; contract asserts `force` (str, `--force[=<reason>]`) + reason + caused_by + ref + close_class; `force_close` excluded.
- scratchy-leprous-galago (bug, CERTIFIED) — MCP parity; force is the reason-carrying str delegating to the normalized lib.
- linen-contrived-wisent (task, depends_on scratchy) — docs.

compiled_state.description:
Add a code-review **surface-parity** overlay: a Pass-1 specialist reviewer for the
four-pass code-review gate that flags when a write-op's parameter / guard / required-field
surface changes on ONE adapter (lib `_lib_writes.py`, CLI `_commands/`, MCP `_mcp_writes.py`)
without the sibling surfaces being updated in lockstep. This is the STATIC code-review
complement to the runtime behavioral conformance oracle landed under topaz-blubbery-mice: the
oracle proves parity at test time; this overlay coaches an author (at review time) toward
parity BEFORE the code lands, catching the escaped-bug class recorded on cranial-goodly-seahog
(a guard/arg added to one entry point and not mirrored to its siblings; worst case
halfwhite-chordal-stonefly had 9 prior PASS reviews with zero findings).

Advisory-first (blocking_enabled=false): a divergence is a coach-not-block finding, verified in
Pass-2 and decided in Pass-3. A DELIBERATE divergence the author justifies must NOT fire (the
reviewer prompt carries that false-positive guard).

## Approach

Model it on the existing GLOB-triggered overlays (api-compat, security): the overlay fires when
the diff touches a known write-surface adapter file, and the LLM reviewer judges whether an
actual param/guard/required-field surface changed and whether the sibling adapters were updated
in lockstep. No change to `registry.content_triggered_overlays` is needed; glob routing via
`applies_to` keeps the overlay inert on unrelated diffs.

1. New packaged reviewer prompt `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-surface-parity.md`
   (front-matter `dimension: code-review-surface-parity`,
   `langfuse_prompt: rebar-code-review-surface-parity`, `outputs: code_review_findings`,
   `execution_mode: agentic`, `category: code-review-pass`), matching the deletion-impact /
   api-compat contract (evidence-record findings, `criteria: ["surface-parity"]`, no
   model-emitted severity). The prompt enumerates the three write surfaces, tells the reviewer
   to Grep the sibling adapters for the changed param/guard, and carries the false-positive
   guards (deliberate justified divergence; a purely internal refactor changing no
   caller-visible surface; an adapter-bound param such as `_creation_channel` / `return_alias` /
   `source` / `repo_root` that is intentionally not caller-visible).
2. Add `"surface-parity"` to `OVERLAY_IDS` in `src/rebar/llm/code_review/registry.py` (closed
   enum; comment it glob-triggered, advisory).
3. Add the routing entry to `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`:
   `exec: AGENT`, `applies_to` globbing the write-surface adapters
   (`**/_commands/**`, `**/_lib_writes.py`, `**/_mcp_writes.py`), `default_posture: advisory`,
   `block_threshold: 0.95`, `blocking_enabled: false`, `_comment` citing this ticket.
4. Wire the overlay into the four-pass gate topology so the finder is actually DISPATCHED:
   - `src/rebar/llm/reviewers/code-review-base.md` — add a `- `surface-parity` — …` bullet to
     the FIXED overlay catalog (base reviewer's `recommend_overlays` escalation list). A strict
     no-drift test (`test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids`) requires the catalog
     to EXACTLY equal `OVERLAY_IDS`, so this edit is mandatory the moment the id is added.
   - `src/rebar/llm/workflow/gates/code-review.yaml` — add a
     `{ prompt: code-review-surface-parity, when: "${{ steps.triggers.outputs.include_surface_parity }}" }`
     entry to the `round_a` batch and its
     `steps.union.outputs.include_surface_parity` twin to the `round_b` batch, mirroring the
     two existing `code-review-deletion-impact` entries. Without this the `include_surface_parity`
     glob flag flips but no finder runs.
5. `reviewers/index.json` needs NO change: overlay prompts (category `code-review-pass`,
   `is_reviewer` false) are excluded from the selection catalog, so
   `prompts.regenerate_prompt_index()` is a no-op — the drift gate stays green because the
   prompt is correctly ABSENT (like every sibling overlay), not registered.

## Portability

The overlay is part of rebar's IN-PROCESS code-review gate (`rebar review-code` /
`produce_code_review_verdict`); it runs via the same library entry point on every platform with
NO dependency on any specific CI provider (identical with a diverse CI provider or no CI
provider). Registration is data + a packaged prompt, loaded in-process. This satisfies
`project.portability`.

## Scope

- ADD reviewer prompt `code-review-surface-parity.md`.
- EDIT `registry.py` (`OVERLAY_IDS`), `criteria_routing.json` (routing entry),
  `code-review-base.md` (catalog bullet), `code-review.yaml` (round_a + round_b finder).
- index.json is NOT touched (overlays are excluded from the catalog; regen is a no-op).
- ADD tests (see Testing).

OUT OF SCOPE: flipping the overlay to blocking (advisory-first by design; a later calibration
ticket may promote it, mirroring cranial-goodly-seahog); any change to the runtime oracle
(topaz); any change to the write adapters themselves (scratchy/blusterous own those).

## Testing

- Unit: assert `"surface-parity"` is a member of `OVERLAY_IDS` and that
  `registry.routing_index()["surface-parity"]` has the expected shape
  (`exec == "AGENT"`, advisory, `blocking_enabled is False`, `block_threshold == 0.95`, and the
  three write-surface globs present).
- Unit: assert `registry.threshold_for(["surface-parity"])` resolves to `(0.95, False)`
  (advisory, non-blocking) — it does NOT join the approved blocking set.
- Unit: assert the glob routing FIRES the overlay for a changed
  `src/rebar/_commands/transition.py` (and `_mcp_writes.py`) and stays inert for an unrelated
  file (e.g. a docs-only change), via the existing overlay-selection seam
  (`overlay_union` / `workflow_ops`).
- Drift: assert the base-reviewer catalog stays in lockstep with `OVERLAY_IDS`
  (`test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids` passes with the new bullet).
- Workflow: assert the `code-review-surface-parity` finder is actually DISPATCHED in the
  `round_a` batch for a changed `src/rebar/_commands/*.py` (not merely that the
  `include_surface_parity` flag flips), mirroring the deletion-impact workflow test.
- Drift: assert `reviewers/index.json` is UNCHANGED — the overlay (category
  `code-review-pass`) is excluded from the catalog, so regen output is byte-identical and the
  drift gate passes as a no-op.
- `make lint` + `make typecheck` green; the complexity ratchet unaffected (no function grows).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] A new `surface-parity` overlay exists in the code-review gate: `"surface-parity"` is a
      member of `OVERLAY_IDS` and has a routing entry in `criteria_routing.json`.
- [x] The overlay is GLOB-triggered on the three write-surface adapters
      (`_commands/`, `_lib_writes.py`, `_mcp_writes.py`) and stays inert on unrelated diffs, and
      is WIRED into the round_a/round_b batches of the code-review gate so the finder is actually
      dispatched (not just an unused include flag).
- [x] The base-reviewer overlay catalog (`code-review-base.md`) lists `surface-parity`, keep
      `test_base_prompt_enumerates_exactly_the_overlay_ids` green.
- [x] The overlay is ADVISORY (`blocking_enabled: false`, `block_threshold: 0.95`);
      `threshold_for(["surface-parity"])` == `(0.95, False)` and it is NOT in the approved
      blocking set.
- [x] A packaged reviewer prompt `code-review-surface-parity.md` exists (deletion-impact/api-
      compat contract); `reviewers/index.json` stays UNCHANGED (overlays excluded), drift gate a
      no-op.
- [x] The reviewer prompt carries the false-positive guards (deliberate justified divergence;
      adapter-bound non-caller-visible params; internal-only refactors) so a compliant lockstep
      change or a justified divergence returns no finding.
- [x] Unit tests in `tests/unit/test_code_review_surface_parity.py` assert the overlay
      membership, routing, glob firing on each write adapter, and round_a/round_b dispatch.
